subtitle: Three templates for Internet-Drafts that contain MIB module definitions.

tldr.problem: Editors reused older MIB documents as templates, but boilerplate and required sections can change over time.
tldr.mechanism: The MIB Doctors directorate provides three annotated templates: XML for XML2RFC users, text with embedded advice, and plain text without advice.
tldr.outcome: The templates aim to make MIB documents more uniform and easier to read and review. RFC 5249 is a Best Current Practice.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 5249 as a Best Current Practice and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It references templates for MIB module documents.

sections.title: Why Use MIB Templates
sections.content:
RFC 5249 references annotated templates for IETF documents containing MIB module definitions. The goal is to reduce editors' work and make the documents more uniform, readable, and reviewable.

Editors had often used older MIB documents as starting points, but required boilerplate and other elements change over time. The templates were made available on the IETF Tools website and could be updated as requirements changed.
sections.plainLanguage: A current template is safer than copying an older document whose required sections may have changed. The templates help authors present MIB documents consistently.

sections.title: The Three Template Forms
sections.content:
The MIB Doctors directorate produced three templates for Internet-Drafts containing MIB modules. One is XML for editors using XML2RFC and includes advice in comments. A second is text with advice embedded in the document. A third is plain text without advice.

The templates include required boilerplate and sections about a MIB module's purpose, organization, and relationship to other modules. The memo notes that many MUST statements in the templates echo IESG requirements for Internet-Drafts.
sections.plainLanguage: Authors can choose XML with comments, text with advice, or plain text without advice. All three provide a consistent document structure.

sections.title: The MIB Module Itself
sections.content:
The templates do not include a template for the MIB module itself. Validation tools typically require the module to be separate from the surrounding document, so the MIB Doctors suggest developing it separately and then including it in the document.

The memo recommends that editors read RFC 4181 for MIB author and reviewer guidance. The templates do not directly affect network security, though they include boilerplate and advice for a MIB document's Security Considerations section.
sections.plainLanguage: The template covers the document around the MIB module, not the module's code itself. The module should be prepared separately and then added to the document.
